question: The H.C.F. and the L.C.M. of two numbers are 3 and 672, respectively. If one of the numbers is 96, find the other one.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any two numbers, the product of the numbers equals the product of their H.C.F. and L.C.M.

Other Number = (H.C.F. × L.C.M.) ÷ First Number

Other Number = (3 × 672) ÷ 96

Other Number = 2016 ÷ 96 = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

H.C.F. of the two numbers = 3

L.C.M. of the two numbers = 672

First number = 96

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = H.C.F. × L.C.M.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the second number be x.

⇒ 96 × x = 3 × 672

⇒ 96 × x = 2016

⇒ x = 2016 ÷ 96

⇒ x = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule for HCF and LCM

For any two positive integers a and b, the product of their HCF and LCM is strictly equal to the product of the numbers themselves: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. This rule does not apply to three or more numbers.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is 1. For any two co-prime numbers, their LCM is directly equal to their product.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF of fractions = (HCF of numerators) ÷ (LCM of denominators)
LCM of fractions = (LCM of numerators) ÷ (HCF of denominators)
